memos.headline: GOOGL and CAT Lead on Relative Strength; MSFT and UNH in Technical Distress
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. GOOGL is trading within 0.1% of its 52-week high with +75% 26-week return and dominant relative strength vs SPY (+17.9% over 12 weeks), while CAT sits just 1.2% off its high with +51.6% over 26 weeks and similarly strong relative performance. On the other side, MSFT is down 20.6% from its 52-week high with RSI at 32.6 and deeply negative relative strength (-18.0% vs SPY over 12 weeks)—this is a broken trend, not a buying opportunity yet. UNH is the most alarming chart in the group: down 52.1% from its high, RSI at 32.5, and last week alone lost 19.5%—this is a falling knife with no sign of stabilization. XOM is at its 52-week high with RSI at 80.6, which is overbought enough to warrant caution despite the strong trend; I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50-day mean before adding.

views.note: Trading at 52-week highs with RSI 65.7 and massive relative strength (+17.9% vs SPY over 12w); would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~$318).
Just 1.2% off highs with +13.9% 12-week relative strength vs SPY and RSI 62.6 still below overbought; invalidation level is a close below ~$600 (roughly the 50-day area).

Broken downtrend with price 9.6% below 50-day and 11.5% below 200-day mean, RSI 32.6, and -18% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks; would reconsider only on a reclaim of the 200-day average (~$486).
Down 52% from highs with a 19.5% drop last week alone, RSI 32.5, and ATR at 4.69%—this is a falling knife with extreme volatility; no technical reason to step in until price stabilizes above $310.
Trend is powerful (+24.3% over 12w, at 52-week high) but RSI at 80.6 is extremely overbought and 15.4% above the 50-day mean screams mean-reversion risk; would go long on a pullback toward $125-$130.

Sitting above both moving averages with RSI 57.3 but 12-week relative strength vs SPY is -8.9%, suggesting the broader AI leadership may be fading; needs a breakout above $206 (52-week high area) to turn bullish.
Mildly above both averages with neutral RSI at 52.9 but 12-week relative strength vs SPY is -7.1%; no strong directional signal, watching for a break above $254 or below $225.
Bounced 4.6% this week but still 3.3% below the 50-day mean and showing -6.0% 4-week relative strength vs SPY; needs to reclaim $268 (50-day area) to turn constructive.
Mild pullback with RSI 44.4 and price near the 50-day mean, but 4-week relative strength of -6.5% vs SPY is concerning; would get interested on a hold above $295 and RSI turning up.
Quiet positive relative strength (+4.4% vs SPY over 4w) and low ATR of 1.56% make it a defensive hold, but still 13.9% off highs and below the 200-day mean; not compelling enough for a long.

memos.headline: MSFT and NVDA Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse and XOM Revenue Decline Warrant Caution
memos.body: I am most convicted on MSFT and NVDA as durable earnings compounders. MSFT's December quarter showed $81.27B revenue (+16.7% YoY) with a stunning 47.3% net margin and net income up 59.5% YoY on only $40.26B total debt — this is best-in-class operating leverage. NVDA printed $57.01B revenue (+62.5% YoY) at a 56.0% net margin with minimal leverage ($8.47B debt), confirming the AI capex cycle is still flowing through to the bottom line. On the other side, UNH's net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on a razor-thin 2.1% net margin despite 12.2% revenue growth, signaling severe cost or reserve pressures that I cannot underwrite until I see stabilization. XOM's revenue declined 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3%, and at an 8.8% net margin the earnings trajectory is clearly negative — I need to see commodity price recovery or cost restructuring before getting constructive.

views.note: 47.3% net margin on 16.7% revenue growth with manageable $40.26B debt is the strongest earnings quality in the universe; would reassess if cloud segment growth decelerates below 20%.
62.5% YoY revenue growth at 56.0% net margin with only $8.47B debt reflects extraordinary pricing power; a gross margin compression below 70% would change my view.
$102.35B revenue growing 15.9% YoY with 34.2% net margin and low $14.79B debt shows durable ad and cloud earnings; would turn cautious if search revenue share erodes.
Revenue of $180.17B (+13.4% YoY) with net margin expanding to 11.8% and net income up 38.2% shows operating leverage kicking in; margin sustainability is the key variable.
Revenue grew 7.9% to $102.47B with a healthy 26.8% margin, but $90.68B total debt is the highest in the group and top-line growth is modest relative to peers.
Solid 31.0% net margin and 8.8% revenue growth, but bank-specific leverage ($427.2B debt) and cyclical credit risk keep me from taking a strong directional view.
Only 1.5% revenue growth and a 6.7% net income decline to $4.32B suggest limited near-term earnings momentum despite defensive positioning.
Revenue grew 9.5% but net income fell 6.7% to $2.30B, implying margin pressure; need to see cost discipline before getting constructive.
Net income down 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on a 2.1% net margin despite 12.2% revenue growth signals a fundamental margin problem I cannot underwrite.
Revenue declining 5.2% with net income down 12.3% and an 8.8% net margin points to deteriorating earnings power tied to commodity weakness.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Sticky Inflation and Rising Long Rates Favor Banks Over Pure Duration Plays
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime—the upper bound has fallen 75 bp over the past year to 3.75%, with 50 bp of that in the last three months alone—yet the cycle is maturing. CPI is running at +2.7% y/y with a 0.6% three-month gain (roughly 2.4% annualized), which is close enough to target to keep cuts on the table but not fast enough to justify aggressive further easing. Unemployment at 4.40% is stable over three months but up 30 bp y/y, signaling a mild softening rather than outright deterioration. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply to +71 bp (+37 bp y/y), a classic late-easing/early-recovery signal that benefits banks' net interest margins while the 15 bp rise in the 10y over three months to 4.26% pressures long-duration growth multiples. A CPI print above 3% or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would force me to revisit this regime call.

views.note: Steepening curve (+37 bp y/y in 10y-2y spread) and still-elevated short rates support NIM expansion for large banks.
Duration-sensitive mega-cap faces headwind from the 15 bp rise in the 10y over three months, though the broader easing cycle provides a floor.
Similar duration dynamics to AAPL; rising long yields temper multiple expansion even as the Fed eases.
Highest-duration name in the universe is most exposed to the recent backup in the 10y; I lack conviction until long rates stabilize.
Mild labor-market softening without recession and an easing Fed historically support cyclical capex names; steepening curve confirms expansion expectations.
Staples lose their defensive bid in a soft-landing regime; 2.7% CPI supports pricing power but steepening curve rotates flows toward cyclicals and banks.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst—inflation is moderate, not accelerating—and the mild slowdown in labor markets doesn't scream demand boom.
Consumer-facing cyclical benefits from stable employment and easing rates; less pure-duration risk than NVDA given diversified revenue.
Ad-driven revenue is cyclically sensitive but the 10y backup limits multiple expansion; waiting for clearer direction in long rates.
Defensive healthcare is less macro-driven; no strong signal from current rate or labor data to take a directional view.

memos.headline: Earnings-Season Sentiment Divergence: MSFT and UNH Crushed, CAT and PG Shine
memos.body: I am reading this week's price reactions to earnings 8-Ks as the clearest sentiment signal of the cycle so far. MSFT dropped 10.0% on its Jan-28 results filing, and UNH cratered 19.6% on its Jan-27 report—both moves suggest deeply negative narrative shifts that are unlikely to be fully digested in a single session and could attract further negative media coverage. On the positive side, CAT rallied 3.4% on its Jan-29 earnings release and PG gained 2.6% on its Jan-22 results, indicating constructive sentiment that may have room to build. AAPL's muted +0.5% reaction to its Jan-29 earnings filing tells me the market had already priced in expectations, leaving sentiment roughly neutral. I have low conviction on names like NVDA and XOM where we lack fresh earnings-driven price signals and only have governance filings to work with.

views.note: A 10% post-earnings drop signals a severe negative narrative shift that likely has further to run in media tone.
A 19.6% single-day earnings selloff is an extreme negative sentiment event; I expect continued adverse coverage pressure.
The +3.4% earnings-day pop suggests a positive sentiment inflection that could attract further buying interest.
Solid +2.6% reaction to Q2 results and supportive Reg FD disclosures point to constructive and durable positive tone.
A mere +0.5% move on earnings suggests sentiment was already priced; no clear directional edge here.
The -4.2% earnings reaction on Jan-13 was negative but has had over two weeks to be absorbed; sentiment likely stabilizing.
Only a director change filing with no earnings reaction data—insufficient signal to form a sentiment view.
Reg FD and governance filings provide no meaningful sentiment catalyst; awaiting earnings for a clearer read.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Retreating but VIX Spike and Rising Oil Signal Residual Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 44% over the past month to 248.94, suggesting that a recent wave of policy anxiety—likely tied to trade or sanctions rhetoric—has partially unwound, though the level remains elevated in absolute terms. At the same time, VIX has jumped nearly 19% month-over-month to 16.88, and WTI crude is up 11.9% to $64.77/bbl over the same period, which I read as the market pricing in a discrete geopolitical or supply-side risk event rather than broad macro deterioration (HY OAS actually tightened 10bp on the month). The steepening yield curve (+22bp over 3 months to 0.71pp) is consistent with fiscal expansion or tariff-driven inflation expectations rather than recession fears. I have moderate conviction that names with heavy China/export-control exposure (NVDA, AAPL) carry asymmetric downside from any re-escalation, while energy (XOM) and domestic infrastructure plays (CAT) benefit from the current supply-tightening and fiscal backdrop. A formal broadening of semiconductor export controls or new sanctions on Russian/Iranian crude would be the catalysts that change my views.

views.note: Semiconductor export controls remain the key structural overhang; any tightening of China AI-chip restrictions would hit revenue disproportionately, and the elevated VIX suggests the market senses near-term policy risk.
Supply-chain concentration in China is a persistent geopolitical vulnerability, but the sharp drop in policy uncertainty over the past month reduces the probability of imminent tariff escalation.

WTI up 11.9% m/m to $64.77 likely reflects geopolitical supply risk (sanctions enforcement or OPEC+ discipline); XOM's recent Reg FD filing suggests forward guidance is being updated in a supportive price environment.

A steepening curve and elevated but declining policy uncertainty favor domestic capex and infrastructure spending; CAT's 1/29 Reg FD disclosure may reflect updated demand signals consistent with this backdrop.
Steeper curve is a tailwind for net interest income, but two 8-K filings in January (including an 8.01 Other Events) introduce uncertainty I cannot resolve from available evidence alone.
Defensive consumer staples face margin pressure if tariff-driven input costs rise, but the sharp decline in policy uncertainty reduces that tail risk for now.
